summary.name: Azure AI Apps and Agents
summary.one_liner: Microsoft Azure's product overview page for its AI platform, covering Microsoft Foundry for building, governing, and deploying AI apps and agents, plus the related Azure data, developer, and security services.
use_cases: Building and deploying enterprise AI apps and agents
Choosing among thousands of AI models from a model catalog
Adding retrieval-augmented generation to apps with databases
Monitoring, evaluating, and securing generative AI applications
Automating developer workflows with AI agents
Running AI models locally on Windows or macOS devices
summary.what_it_does: The page is a marketing-style overview of Microsoft's Azure AI offerings. It lists Microsoft Foundry as the core platform for building AI apps and agents, with access to more than 11,000 models, agent and multi-agent orchestration, tracing and debugging tools, and evaluations and safety filters. It also describes supporting Azure services: managed databases (PostgreSQL, Cosmos DB, SQL Database) with native vector search, Kubernetes and App Service for hosting, GitHub Copilot for development, and Defender for Cloud and Foundry Control Plane for security and governance. Customer stories and resource links to tutorials and architecture guides are included, but the page gives few technical specifics on pricing or limits.
notable: Access to more than 11,000 models from providers including Microsoft, OpenAI, DeepSeek, Mistral, Meta, and Hugging Face
Foundry Local runs models, agents, and components on Windows and macOS devices with offline access
Native vector search and language models inside Azure managed databases such as PostgreSQL
caveats: Page mentions a free Azure trial of up to 30 days and pay-as-you-go accounts, implying paid usage beyond that
Some listed services are in preview (e.g., Azure HorizonDB), and the page does not detail their limits
Page is mainly marketing; pricing details and technical limits are not stated
